pool.text: Lyon became part of the Kingdom of Arles and the Holy Roman Empire.
Lyon finally came under the direct control of France.
Catholics committed acts of mass violence against Protestant Huguenots in Lyon.
The Bourse treasury building was constructed to resemble an open-air bazaar.
Revolutionary armies besieged the city until it surrendered in October.
A French Directory commissioner was assassinated in Lyon shortly after a coup.
The Brothers of the Sacred Heart Roman Catholic congregation was founded.
The canuts silk workers staged their first major uprising for better pay.
The large urban park known as Parc de la Tête d'or was established.
The 1st Free French Division and resistance forces liberated the city.
The commune of Saint-Rambert-l'Île-Barbe was annexed into the fifth arrondissement.
The fifth arrondissement was split to create the ninth and final arrondissement.
A museum dedicated to automated puppets opened its doors in Vieux Lyon.
The historic urban site of Lyon gained official UNESCO World Heritage status.
Graffiti artists Birdy Kids began decorating random buildings and ring road walls.
The Birdy Kids artist collective was chosen to serve as cultural ambassadors.
The Musée des Confluences opened its doors to display anthropology and sciences.
Lyon and suburban municipalities formed the Metropolis of Lyon governing authority.
The Globalization and World Rankings Research Institute classified Lyon as a Beta city.
The metropolitan council was directly elected by universal suffrage for the first time.
